text:
maria: noticing a big throughput drop in dedicated-gpu-pool-west around 20:54 UTC, lots of worker restarts and OOMs. p99 generation latency shot up from ~300ms to 2.1s.
kevin: put up graphs — looks like a sharp step at 20:54, correlate with kernel selection changes?
maria: I checked the rollout log, no config rollout at that time. But the runtime did auto-fallback kernels on several hosts.
jin: noisy-tenant on node gpu-17 had a large mem spike ~20:53, saw frequent page reclaim. Could be fragmentation ripple.
perf-ron: profiler snapshot attached (low-noise sample): heap fragmentation increased ~x3 and KV cache hit rate dropped ~12%. Workers restarted due to CUDA OOM on small batches.
ops-simon: @sre-bot did any autoscaler events fire?
sre-bot: autoscaler: added 2 nodes to dedicated-gpu-pool-west at 20:56 (triggered by CPU pressure), no explicit drain events recorded.
maria: here's the rough diagnostics I ran:
```
# top problematic errors from runtime logs
grep -A2 "CUDA out of memory" /var/log/redwood/runtime/*.log | head -n 20
---
2026-01-11T20:54:03Z runtime[worker-203]: ERROR: CUDA out of memory allocating 256MB KV cache slab
2026-01-11T20:54:05Z runtime[worker-204]: INFO: kernel_fallback: switched kernel from opt_attn_v2 to safe_attn_v1 (reason=alloc_fail)
2026-01-11T20:54:09Z runtime[worker-203]: WARN: worker_restart signal: oom
```

# nvidia-smith (condensed)
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-mem.csv
... lines show repeating spikes then drop as workers restart
```
kevin: interesting — kernel fallback triggered because alloc failed, but fallback path appears to allocate a larger temporary buffer for safe_attn_v1 on some shapes which exacerbates fragmentation.
perf-ron: that matches profiling: fallback increases transient allocation count (per-token) by ~18 allocations per layer, bumps working set by ~30MB on our 16k-vocab models. If KV cache eviction policy also runs concurrently, we thrash.
maria: action items I'm running now:
- disable automatic kernel fallback on dedicated-gpu-pool-west (temp mitigation)
- bump KV cache eviction aggressiveness for the pool (reduce max_cached_prefix to 6k tokens)
- schedule full dmesg+heap profiling on impacted hosts
jin: I'm doing a targeted drain of noisy tenant workloads on gpu-17 to reduce allocation churn.
ops-simon: rolling rollback of heuristic deployed to runtime yesterday?
kevin: checked canary: there was a kernel-selection heuristic tweak deployed ~18:30 that widened acceptable shape-matching to prefer opt_attn_v2 more aggressively. Not a rollback yet.
perf-ron: hypothesizing sequence: noisy tenant causes page churn -> alloc attempts trigger kernel fallback path for some shards -> fallback uses different buffer layout causing higher live allocation -> KV cache eviction & small-batch surges cause slab fragmentation -> OOM + restarts -> throughput drop.
maria: quick mitigation status: disabling fallback removed repeated OOMs within 6 minutes, p95 latency trending back down. throughput still ~7% below baseline due to some worker restarts.
jin: collecting heapprof dumps; attaching set of pmap outputs.
kevin: longer-term fixes to consider:
- ensure kernel fallback path preallocates from pooled allocator to avoid transient fragmentation
- change fallback to prefer kernels with lower peak temporary footprint, not just success rate
- add an allocation-safety check before switching kernels (if memory headroom < X, avoid fallback)
- improve KV cache eviction backpressure so eviction doesn't run concurrently with fallback-induced spikes
perf-ron: also worth tuning slab GC sweep frequency; fragmentation grows when sweep interval is too long under churn. We can lower sweep interval for high-churn pools.
ops-simon: can we add a rule to autoscaler to scale by GPU memory pressure signals (not only CPU/GPU utilization)?
maria: noted. For incident report I'm going to collect: kernel-selection logs, per-host allocation histograms, kv-cache eviction traces, heap snapshots, and p99/p50 latency windows.
kevin: will file a follow-up postmortem with root cause hypothesis + timeline.
jin: temporary note: if you see residual OOMs, run `sudo systemctl stop redwood-runtime && echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` on impacted hosts to speed recovery (manual, non-ideal).
perf-ron: adding perf regression test: replay noisy-tenant traffic in staging with fallback enabled to see fragmentation delta.
maria: thanks everyone. tagging @oncall for visibility. :eyes: :thumbsup:
kevin: great, let's keep this thread as the single source for updates and add traced artifacts as comments.
